topic: Manual click rate limit for large-field lag
currentUserGoal: Reduce lag when the player rapidly smashes left click on a large visible field, while keeping clicks feeling responsive.
changesMade: Added a high manual tile-click rate limiter in GameScene.ts: normal manual clicks allow roughly 29 accepted touches per second, tightening to roughly 24 per second while the board is busy, frame spikes were seen, or manual click pressure is active.

Added a one-second manual click pressure detector. After 12 manual attempts in the window, pressure stays active briefly so visual feedback reuses the existing ambient budgets for pop text, transient objects, and particle bursts.
Kept persistent-touch upgrade input and the built-in perf harness tap burst out of the manual limiter so their existing timing and benchmark behavior remain stable.

knownIssues: The manual click-pressure cap needs subjective testing on the user's real save and mouse. The current cap is intentionally high: it should only trim extreme bursts.

Browser automation coordinate clicks were too slow to reproduce true physical click mashing. The standard harness and a real input smoke passed, but a human live test remains the best final feel check.
nextRecommendedSteps: Run the live/dev build on the user's real save at the screenshot-sized field and aggressively left-click for 20-30 seconds.
If it still lags, lower MANUAL_TOUCH_BUSY_MIN_INTERVAL_MS slightly upward from 42ms or make manual pressure activate earlier than 12 attempts per second.
If clicks feel capped too early, raise MANUAL_TOUCH_PRESSURE_THRESHOLD before changing the accepted-click intervals.
